**Headquarters:** **Pulicat** till **1689-90** – the Dutch capital and Governor's seat on the Coromandel and in Andhra; **Nagapattinam** after 1690 – HQ of the Dutch settlements in India.

1.x: **Trading centres:** Nagapattinam, Chinsura, Machilipatnam, Surat, Broach, Agra, Cochin, Ahmedabad, Patna, Kasimbazar, Balasore.
**Bengal:** **Chinsurah** was Dutch; Bandel and Hooghly were Portuguese, **Serampore (Srirampur)** Danish.
**Kochi:** the Dutch took it from the Portuguese (**1663**) and rebuilt the fort (**Fort Williams**, Fort Kochi); it passed to the **British in 1795** (1814 treaty).
**Mattancherry Palace** (Kochi) – Portuguese gift (c. 1555) to the Raja of Cochin, renovated by the Dutch → **"Dutch Palace"**.

2.x: **Why the Dutch failed:** **English rivalry** (Amboyna 1623; **1667 compromise** – the Dutch withdrew from India for Indonesia), the defeat at Bedara, and their priority on the **Indonesian spice trade**; by **1795** the English had expelled them.
**Anglo-Dutch conferences of 1613 and 1615** failed to end the rivalry.
**Anglo-Dutch Treaty 1824:** remaining posts (Pulicat, Chinsura) to the British by **1825**; Dutch presence in India **1605-1825**.

3.x: **VOC (Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie):** **20 March 1602**; the **States-General** merged several companies; powers to **wage war, make treaties, acquire territory, build forts**.
**Background:** **Philip II**'s ban on Lisbon; **Linschoten**'s *Itinerario*; **Cornelis de Houtman** reached **Sumatra and Bantam (1596)**.
**Asian HQ:** **Batavia (Jakarta)**; the spice islands came first, India was a cloth depot.
**Trade:** Coromandel textiles for spices; **indigo**, raw **silk**, cotton cloth, **saltpetre (Bihar)**, opium and rice; silk and porcelain imported.

**Andhra:** first Europeans in Andhra to **mint coins**; Pulicat a hub of the **slave trade to Batavia**; network from **Machilipatnam to Bheemunipatnam** (Draksharama, Palakollu, Narsapur, Jagannathapuram).
